research.topic: quality-coverage-measure: scan quality/coverage estimation, measurement confidence, snapping, thermal/battery for an iPhone LiDAR mapper (iOS 18 target, Xcode 26.6 / iOS 26 SDK)

facts.claim: RoomCaptureSession.Instruction has exactly six cases: normal, moveCloseToWall, moveAwayFromWall, turnOnLight, slowDown, lowTexture. Delivered via the delegate. lowTexture fires when the user points at a solid-color wall or the viewfinder has no wall edges/defining shapes. Apple does not publish the distance/speed/lux thresholds behind the other cases (its ML guidance model is ~90% accurate for lighting/distance/speed per Apple ML research).
facts.api:
enum RoomCaptureSession.Instruction { case normal; case moveCloseToWall; case moveAwayFromWall; case turnOnLight; case slowDown; case lowTexture }
protocol RoomCaptureSessionDelegate: AnyObject { func captureSession(_ session: RoomCaptureSession, didProvide instruction: RoomCaptureSession.Instruction) }
facts.notes: All six cases and the delegate signature read from the doc JSON this session. Instruction only says what to do, not a numeric quality; treat non-.normal instructions as a live quality flag and log their duration to compute a 'coached time' ratio per scan.

facts.claim: CapturedRoom.Surface.completedEdges is a Set of the surface's edges (top/bottom/left/right) that RoomPlan considers finished; a wall missing .left/.right means RoomPlan never saw that end (the wall ends at the observation boundary, not at a real corner). Apple's doc metadata lists it as iOS 16.0, not 17.0 as the task assumed; polygonCorners and Section are the iOS 17 additions.
facts.availability: completedEdges/Edge: iOS 16.0+ per doc JSON; polygonCorners: iOS 17.0+
facts.notes: Declaration and platforms verified from JSON. The semantics ('edge was completed = observed') are only community evidence (github.com/galmadar/RoomDesigner PR #13 uses walls whose completedEdges lack left/right as a 'you passed it quickly' warning); Apple's abstract just says 'edges that outline the surface'. Use: wall coverage score = completedEdges.count/4, and flag walls with fewer than 4 edges or confidence != .high.

facts.claim: CapturedRoom.Confidence (high/medium/low) is per Surface and per Object and expresses certainty in the CATEGORY classification of that element, not its dimensional accuracy.
facts.notes: Doc overview: 'a level of certainty in the surface's category'. Do not present it as measurement accuracy; use it as a weight (high=1.0, medium=0.7, low=0.4) in the per-wall quality score.

facts.claim: CapturedRoom.Surface geometry needed for expected-area and snapping: transform (simd_float4x4, plane position/orientation), dimensions (simd_float3 bounding box: x=width, y=height, z=thickness), parentIdentifier (door/window/opening -> owning wall), category, curve (optional), story. CapturedRoom groups them as walls/doors/windows/openings/floors (floors iOS 17) plus objects and sections.
facts.notes: Wall corner points in world space = transform * (±dimensions.x/2, ±dimensions.y/2, 0, 1) when polygonCorners is empty; otherwise transform * (corner.x, corner.y, corner.z, 1). Expected wall area = dimensions.x*dimensions.y (or polygon area) minus the areas of doors/windows/openings whose parentIdentifier == wall.identifier.

facts.claim: RoomCaptureSession delivers live CapturedRoom updates (didAdd/didChange/didUpdate/didRemove) during the scan, a final CapturedRoomData on didEndWith, and exposes/accepts an ARSession. Errors include deviceTooHot, exceedSceneSizeLimit, worldTrackingFailure. stop(pauseARSession:) (iOS 17) keeps the ARSession alive between rooms.
facts.notes: All delegate methods have default implementations. Architectural point: because you can pass your own ARSession and set its ARSessionDelegate, you can read ARFrame.sceneDepth, ARCamera.trackingState, lightEstimate and ARMeshAnchors from the same camera stream RoomPlan is using. Whether RoomPlan's internal ARWorldTrackingConfiguration already enables sceneReconstruction/.sceneDepth is NOT documented; log session.arSession.configuration in captureSession(_:didStartWith:) on the first CI build (see open questions).

facts.claim: ARCamera.trackingState and ARFrame.worldMappingStatus are the free per-frame tracking-quality signals. TrackingState.Reason has 4 cases; WorldMappingStatus has 4 cases. Tracking changes also arrive through ARSessionObserver.session(_:cameraDidChangeTrackingState:).
facts.notes: worldMappingStatus semantics from doc: limited = area around current position not yet mapped; extending = recently visited areas mapped, still mapping here; mapped = visible area adequately mapped. Use: only count coverage observations while trackingState == .normal; record the fraction of frames in .limited for the session's pose-drift term.

facts.claim: ARFrame.sceneDepth / smoothedSceneDepth give an ARDepthData with depthMap (Float32 metres, kCVPixelFormatType_DepthFloat32) and confidenceMap (OneComponent8, one ARConfidenceLevel raw value per pixel: low=0, medium=1, high=2). Enabled by adding .sceneDepth / .smoothedSceneDepth to ARConfiguration.frameSemantics after checking supportsFrameSemantics. Depth is 60 Hz, 256x192 (same aspect as the camera image); LiDAR range is about 5 m; confidence drops on highly reflective or highly absorbing surfaces.
facts.availability: iOS 14.0+ (LiDAR devices only; iPhone 13 Pro Max OK)
facts.notes: Declarations, 60 Hz and the reflective/absorbing caveat verified (doc JSON + WWDC20 10611 transcript). 256x192 and ~5 m range are community/Apple-sample evidence (Apple's point-cloud sample, ARKitScenes, Andy Jazz), not in the API doc: read CVPixelBufferGetWidth at runtime instead of hard-coding. Raw values 0/1/2 follow the ObjC NS_ENUM order; some blogs wrongly say 1..3. Use confidenceMap as the per-observation quality gate and depthMap value as the distance term in the accuracy formula.

facts.claim: ARFrame.lightEstimate.ambientIntensity is the free 'lighting is poor' signal: lumens-scaled value where 1000 = neutral lighting; ambientColorTemperature in Kelvin. ARCamera.exposureDuration and exposureOffset are secondary cues (long exposure = dark or motion blur).
facts.notes: Apple gives no lux mapping. RoomPlan recommends >= 50 lux (WWDC22). Practical thresholds used by AR apps: ambientIntensity < 300 = dark warning, < 600 = dim; calibrate once on device. RoomPlan's .turnOnLight instruction is the authoritative signal while RoomPlan runs; use ambientIntensity for the mesh/object scan modes.

facts.claim: Scene mesh: enable ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.sceneReconstruction = .meshWithClassification (check supportsSceneReconstruction first) and receive ARMeshAnchor via ARSessionDelegate session(_:didAdd:)/session(_:didUpdate:)/session(_:didRemove:). ARMeshGeometry exposes vertices, normals (per face), faces (triangles, ARGeometryElement) and an optional per-face classification buffer (UInt8 raw ARMeshClassification, 0 = .none). Mesh anchors 'constantly update' but are not real-time. ARSession.RunOptions.resetSceneReconstruction clears them. If plane detection is enabled ARKit flattens the mesh on detected planes.
facts.notes: Apple's own per-face classification read (from the doc): classification.buffer.contents().advanced(by: faceIndex).assumingMemoryBound(to: UInt8.self).pointee. Vertex i = buffer.contents() + offset + stride*i as SIMD3<Float>; face i indices = 3 x Int32 at faces.buffer.contents() + i*3*bytesPerIndex (bytesPerIndex is 4). Face area from the three vertices; face centroid quantized to a voxel key is the recommended stable identity, because anchors re-mesh and face indices are not stable across updates. Mesh update cadence (roughly 0.5-1 s per anchor) and anchor block size are community observations only.

facts.claim: ObjectCaptureSession.Feedback has exactly these cases: environmentLowLight, environmentTooDark, movingTooFast, objectNotDetected (iOS 17.4+), objectNotFlippable, objectTooClose, objectTooFar, outOfFieldOfView, overCapturing. There is NO 'outOfRange' case (the task's name is wrong; it is outOfFieldOfView). The session also exposes cameraTracking (normal/limited(reason:)/notAvailable), state, numberOfShotsTaken, maximumNumberOfInputImages, userCompletedScanPass, and AsyncSequence-style *Updates streams.
facts.notes: Doc text: environmentLowLight = auto-capture continues but quality may suffer; environmentTooDark = auto-capture stops; overCapturing = shots beyond maximumNumberOfInputImages are not used on device; userCompletedScanPass flips to true when the capture dial is full and resets on beginNewScanPass/AfterFlip. For the object-scan quality meter use numberOfShotsTaken/maximumNumberOfInputImages plus userCompletedScanPass per pass; Apple's own dial is the coverage UI. ObjectCaptureSession owns the camera; it cannot run concurrently with your ARSession/RoomCaptureSession.

facts.claim: Screen projection for a live coverage overlay: on the iOS 26 SDK (Xcode 26.6) use ARCamera.projectPoint(_:orientation:viewportSize:), ARCamera.projectionMatrix(for:viewportSize:zNear:zFar:) and ARFrame.displayTransform(for:viewportSize:). Apple's doc marks the orientation-based variants deprecated only at iOS 27.0, replaced by viewRotationAngle variants that are iOS 27.0+ and therefore do NOT exist in the iOS 26 SDK. Do not use the viewRotationAngle APIs.
facts.availability: orientation variants iOS 11.0+ (deprecated iOS 27.0); viewRotationAngle variants iOS 27.0+
facts.notes: Doc JSON: projectPoint:orientation:viewportSize: introducedAt 11.0 deprecatedAt 27.0; projectPoint(_:viewRotationAngle:viewportSize:) introducedAt 27.0. For coverage math avoid both: project with intrinsics directly (u = fx*x/z + cx, v = fy*y/z + cy in the 1920x1440 capturedImage space, then scale by 256/1920 to index the depth/confidence map). ARKit camera space: +x along the long device axis, +y up in landscape-right, +z toward the user, so a point in front of the camera has negative z.

facts.claim: ARKit raycasting for snapping/measuring: ARFrame.raycastQuery(from:allowing:alignment:) plus ARSession.raycast(_:) or trackedRaycast; targets estimatedPlane, existingPlaneGeometry, existingPlaneInfinite; ARRaycastResult.worldTransform and anchor. ARPlaneAnchor (iOS 16) gives planeExtent (width/height/rotationOnYAxis), center, classification (wall/floor/ceiling/table/seat/door/window/none) and boundaryVertices for cheap plane-intersection corners when RoomPlan is not running.
facts.availability: raycast iOS 13.0+; planeExtent/ARPlaneExtent iOS 16.0+; plane classification iOS 12.0+
facts.notes: ARPlaneAnchor.extent (simd_float3) still exists but planeExtent is the iOS 16 replacement (the anchor transform is no longer auto-rotated on iOS 16 when the deployment target is >= 16). Raycast against .existingPlaneGeometry for measurement endpoints gives plane-smoothed points (better than raw mesh) and the anchor tells you which wall/floor it hit.

facts.claim: Video format control for thermal/battery mitigation: ARConfiguration.supportedVideoFormats (ordered best first per device), videoFormat (settable), VideoFormat.framesPerSecond / imageResolution / captureDeviceType / isRecommendedForHighResolutionFrameCapturing, videoHDRAllowed, and ARSession.captureHighResolutionFrame for texture stills.
facts.availability: supportedVideoFormats/videoFormat iOS 11.3+; captureDeviceType 14.5+; HDR + high-res capture 16.0+
facts.notes: Read supportedVideoFormats from ARWorldTrackingConfiguration (the base class returns []). Pick the format with framesPerSecond == 30 and the smallest imageResolution when thermalState >= .serious, and re-run the session with that configuration (this restarts the camera; do it between rooms or when the user pauses, not mid-wall). Keep videoHDRAllowed false while scanning. Whether RoomPlan lets you change the video format of its ARSession is untested (see open questions).

facts.claim: Thermal and battery APIs: ProcessInfo.processInfo.thermalState (nominal/fair/serious/critical) with ProcessInfo.thermalStateDidChangeNotification; isLowPowerModeEnabled; UIDevice.current.batteryLevel (requires isBatteryMonitoringEnabled = true); UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled. Apple's guidance for .serious is 'reduce target framerate 60 -> 30, reduce CPU/GPU work, lower detail'; for .critical 'if possible stop using peripherals such as the camera'. RoomPlan additionally ends the session with CaptureError.deviceTooHot.
facts.notes: Verified from doc JSON. Community reports (HackerNoon 'Thermal throttling in real-time AR'): LiDAR+camera+Metal mesh rendering for 10-15 minutes reaches throttle; symptoms are silent (camera frame rate cut, tracking drifts, mesh slides). Apple's own RoomPlan guidance (WWDC22 10127): 'avoid repeated scans or single long scans over 5 minutes' because of battery and thermal issues. Polycam tells users to start at >= 80% battery for multi-room jobs. No published mAh-per-minute figures were found; plan for roughly 1% battery per minute of LiDAR scanning on an iPhone 13 Pro Max as a working assumption and measure it with batteryLevel deltas in the log.

facts.claim: RoomPlan operating envelope from Apple: single room up to 30 x 30 ft (9 x 9 m); max height 3.6 m; lighting >= 50 lux; keep scans under 5 minutes; multi-room (StructureBuilder/CapturedStructure, iOS 17) recommended up to 2,000 sq ft (186 m2) total; difficult: full-height mirrors/glass, very dark surfaces, high ceilings beyond LiDAR range. Apple's RoomPlan detector runs on a local frustum of 7.2 x 4.8 x 3.6 m with 3 cm voxels for walls and reports 95% precision/recall for walls and windows and 90% for doors.
facts.api:
class StructureBuilder { init(options: StructureBuilder.ConfigurationOptions); func capturedStructure(from: [CapturedRoom]) async throws -> CapturedStructure }
struct CapturedStructure { var rooms: [CapturedRoom]; var walls: [CapturedStructure.Surface]; var doors, windows, openings, floors: [CapturedStructure.Surface]; var objects: [CapturedStructure.Object]; var sections: [CapturedStructure.Section] }
facts.notes: Numbers quoted from the WWDC22 (10127) and WWDC23 (10192) transcripts and machinelearning.apple.com/research/roomplan this session. Because RoomPlan's wall voxel grid is 3 cm in-plane, do not claim wall lengths better than about ±3 cm from RoomPlan alone.

facts.claim: Published iPhone LiDAR accuracy: small objects (>10 cm) ±1 cm absolute (Luetzenburg et al., Sci. Rep. 2021, iPhone 12 Pro); point-cloud RMSE vs known shapes 2.05 cm (iPhone 12 Pro) and 2.06 cm (iPhone 15) (Remote Sensing Letters 2026, tandfonline 10.1080/2150704X.2026.2720055); ARKit depth vs Faro ground truth agrees to 3.7 cm median (ARKitScenes analysis, rerun.io); reasonable accuracy up to about 4 m, noisy toward the ~5 m limit; building-scale scans with consumer apps put 69-83% of points within 5 cm of a terrestrial laser scan (iPhone 13 Pro, MDPI 2023); errors grow with distance and with path length because of SLAM drift.
facts.notes: Numbers come from search-result abstracts; the full papers were 403 to WebFetch, so they are 'likely' rather than 'verified'. Additional sources: nature.com/articles/s41598-021-01763-9, mdpi.com/2673-7418/3/4/30, rerun.io/blog/arkitscenes-slam. Apple publishes no accuracy specification for LiDAR, RoomPlan or Measure. Practical framing: per-point depth noise ~0.5-1 cm at 1-2 m, ~2 cm at 3-4 m; room-scale length error 0.5-2% without loop closure.

facts.claim: RoomPlan dimensional accuracy reported by practitioners: per-wall error up to ±5 cm, errors accumulate around a multi-partition space (measured 6.821 m vs true 6.45 m, +37 cm, it-jim); raw RoomPlan/Apple-framework output ±2-4 in across a 20 ft room, e.g. a 30 ft room reading 30 ft 4 in on one wall and 29 ft 9 in on the opposite wall (Scan Manifold, 2026); wall thickness defaults to ~16 cm and walls thicker than ~50 cm become two thin walls; large mirrors create gaps/phantom objects.
facts.notes: Community/vendor evidence, consistent across two independent sources (it-jim, scanmanifold.com). Use it to cap the displayed confidence for RoomPlan-derived lengths: never show better than ±1 in (2.5 cm) for a single wall and scale with wall length.

facts.claim: ARCoachingOverlayView is the stock ARKit coaching UI (goal .tracking/.anyPlane/.horizontalPlane/.verticalPlane/.geoTracking) and can be attached to the RoomPlan ARSession; RoomCaptureSession.Configuration.isCoachingEnabled controls RoomPlan's own coaching. ObjectCaptureSession shows the ARKit coaching overlay automatically when tracking becomes limited.
facts.api:
class ARCoachingOverlayView: UIView { var session: ARSession?; var sessionProvider: (any ARSessionProviding)?; var goal: ARCoachingOverlayView.Goal; var activatesAutomatically: Bool; var isActive: Bool; func setActive(_ active: Bool, animated: Bool); var delegate: (any ARCoachingOverlayViewDelegate)? }
enum ARCoachingOverlayView.Goal: Int { case tracking; case horizontalPlane; case verticalPlane; case anyPlane; case geoTracking }
facts.notes: UIKit view; wrap with UIViewRepresentable. Prefer your own instruction banner driven by RoomCaptureSession.Instruction during room scans and use ARCoachingOverlayView only for the raw-mesh/measure modes.

facts.claim: ARFrame.rawFeaturePoints (ARPointCloud) exists but Apple explicitly says point count/arrangement is unstable between frames and releases; it is only useful as a weak 'texture richness' heuristic (few points = low texture) and for debugging, not as a coverage or accuracy input.
facts.api:
ARFrame: var rawFeaturePoints: ARPointCloud? { get }
class ARPointCloud { var points: [simd_float3]; var identifiers: [UInt64] }
facts.notes: Feature-point count per frame correlates with visual texture; combine with RoomPlan's .lowTexture instruction for the 'aim at textured areas' hint.

gotchas: completedEdges is documented as iOS 16.0 (not 17.0). Its 'observed edge' meaning is undocumented by Apple; treat it as a heuristic and verify on device by scanning half a wall and printing completedEdges in captureSession(_:didUpdate:).
ObjectCaptureSession.Feedback has no `outOfRange`; the case is `outOfFieldOfView`. `objectNotDetected` requires iOS 17.4 (fine with an iOS 18 target). Writing `.outOfRange` costs a CI round trip.

ARCamera.projectPoint(_:viewRotationAngle:viewportSize:) and ARSession.viewRotationAngle are iOS 27 APIs and do not exist in the iOS 26 SDK; the orientation-based projectPoint/unprojectPoint/projectionMatrix/displayTransform are the ones to use and are not deprecated on Xcode 26.6.

ARMeshAnchor face indices are not stable across updates (anchors re-mesh and change vertex/face counts). Keying observation counts by face index will silently reset coverage; key by quantized world-space centroid (voxel hash) instead.

ARDepthData.confidenceMap raw values are 0/1/2 (low/medium/high), the pixel format is 8-bit one-component; the depth map is Float32 metres. Do not hard-code 256x192, read CVPixelBufferGetWidth/Height; on the iPhone 13 Pro Max it is 256x192 at 60 Hz.
confidenceMap is optional (nil when no LiDAR); sceneDepth is nil unless .sceneDepth is in frameSemantics and ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportsFrameSemantics(.sceneDepth) is true.

ARKit camera space has the point in front of the camera at negative z; project with intrinsics using -z (or use the projectionMatrix). Camera image is landscape (1920x1440 on the default format); the depth map has the same aspect ratio, so scale u,v by depthWidth/imageWidth.

Mesh coverage in a 'wall' voxel can be inflated by furniture: only count faces whose ARMeshClassification is .wall (or .floor/.ceiling) when comparing against RoomPlan expected areas, and reject faces whose centroid is more than 10 cm off the RoomPlan wall plane.
RoomPlan's stop() pauses the ARSession by default; call stop(pauseARSession: false) (iOS 17) if you want to keep mesh anchors / world map alive for the next room or for post-scan measuring.

RoomPlan's internal ARWorldTrackingConfiguration is opaque. It is not documented whether it enables sceneReconstruction or the .sceneDepth frame semantic; if your ARSessionDelegate receives no ARMeshAnchors while RoomPlan runs, you cannot re-run the session with your own configuration without breaking RoomPlan (invalidARConfiguration). Plan for a separate mesh pass or run RoomPlan on your own pre-configured ARSession and log the configuration in captureSession(_:didStartWith:) on the first device build.
Changing videoFormat requires session.run(config) again, which restarts the camera and can drop tracking; only do it at natural pauses.

Thermal throttling is silent: no error, no crash; the camera frame rate drops and tracking drifts. RoomPlan surfaces it only at the end as CaptureError.deviceTooHot. Log ProcessInfo.thermalState transitions with timestamps in every session.
UIDevice.batteryLevel returns -1.0 until isBatteryMonitoringEnabled is set to true.

ARFrame retains the camera pixel buffers; keep no more than one ARFrame reference (ARKit stops delivering frames if you hold too many). Copy what you need (camera transform, intrinsics, a downsampled confidence sample) and release the frame.

LiDAR confidence collapses on glass, mirrors, glossy black and strongly back-lit windows; mesh coverage there will stay red no matter how long the user scans. Detect 'persistently low-confidence region near a RoomPlan window' and stop nagging the user.
recommendations: Live coverage algorithm (runs at 3 Hz on a background queue, O(sampled faces)): keep a `[UInt64: UInt8]` voxel hash of 10 cm cells keyed by packed integer (x,y,z) of a face centroid. Every 333 ms take the latest ARFrame (camera transform, intrinsics, imageResolution, confidenceMap), and for each ARMeshAnchor whose bounding box intersects the view frustum, iterate faces with stride 4 (every 4th face): centroid -> camera space; require 0.3 m < -z < 4.0 m, projected (u,v) inside the image, dot(faceNormal, -viewRay) > 0.5 (within 60 deg of facing), and confidenceMap sample at (u*256/1920, v*192/1440) >= medium; then increment the cell's count (saturate at 255). Color per face for the overlay: 0 = red, 1-2 = yellow, >= 3 = green (3 good observations from different frames at 3 Hz means the user lingered about 1 s). Because the hash is keyed by world position it survives ARKit re-meshing. Memory: a 9x9x3 m room at 10 cm cells is at most 243k entries, typically 20-40k.

Expected vs observed area from RoomPlan (1 Hz, only while RoomPlan runs): for each wall, expectedArea = polygon area from polygonCorners (fallback dimensions.x*dimensions.y) minus the areas of doors/windows/openings with parentIdentifier == wall.identifier. observedArea = sum of areas of mesh faces classified .wall whose centroid is within 10 cm of the wall plane and inside the wall rectangle in the wall's local frame (inverse(transform)). wallCoverage = min(1, observed/expected). Room score = area-weighted mean over walls and floors, then multiplied by a quality factor: 1.0 if all four completedEdges and confidence .high, 0.85 if an edge is missing, 0.7 if confidence .medium, 0.5 if .low. Show one number ('Coverage 82%') plus a per-wall list of anything under 70%.

Holes: compute per anchor on session(_:didUpdate:) only (not per frame): build an edge->faceCount map from faces, boundary edges are those with count 1, but discard boundary edges that lie within 2 cm of the anchor's own bounding box faces (anchor seams are not holes). Sum boundary-edge length per 10 cm cell into the same voxel hash as a 'hole' flag and render hole cells in red. Cost is a few ms per updated anchor; skip when thermalState >= .serious.

Per-measurement confidence formula (metres): sigma_depth(d, c) = (0.005 + 0.004*d) * k_c with k_high = 1, k_medium = 1.5, k_low = 3, d = depth of the endpoint when picked; reduce by observations n at the endpoint's cell: sigma_depth / sqrt(min(n, 9)) but never below 0.004. sigma_pose(L) = 0.005*L if every frame during the scan had trackingState == .normal, 0.015*L if any .limited(.excessiveMotion/.insufficientFeatures) occurred, 0.03*L after a relocalization. sigma_pick = 0.003 for a snapped RoomPlan corner with .high confidence, 0.01 for a raycast on plane geometry, 0.02 for a raw mesh vertex. sigma_total = sqrt(sigma_depth_A^2 + sigma_depth_B^2 + sigma_pose^2 + sigma_pick_A^2 + sigma_pick_B^2). Display ±2*sigma_total, floored at 1.0 cm (0.4 in) and rounded up to 0.5 cm / 0.1 in. Wording: 'Estimated accuracy ±0.6 in (typical for iPhone LiDAR; verify critical dimensions with a tape)'. Show a 'Low confidence' badge instead of a number when sigma_total exceeds 4 cm, and cap any RoomPlan-derived wall length at no better than ±2.5 cm.

Snapping order for manual measurements (10 cm world radius or 24 pt screen radius, whichever is smaller in world space): 1) RoomPlan corners: wall polygon corners (transform * polygonCorners, or the four rectangle corners), door/window/opening corners, and computed wall-wall-floor triple intersections (walls whose end points are within 15 cm: intersect the two wall planes with the floor plane taken from floors[0].transform, or y = floor y). 2) ARPlaneAnchor boundaryVertices when RoomPlan is not running. 3) ARRaycastQuery .existingPlaneGeometry hit (plane-smoothed point) with .vertical/.horizontal alignment; 4) fallback .estimatedPlane. Skip mesh crease detection in v1; if needed later, mark a mesh vertex as an edge when the normals of its adjacent faces differ by > 35 deg, precomputed per anchor update.

Thermal/battery ladder: subscribe to ProcessInfo.thermalStateDidChangeNotification. nominal/fair: 60 fps format, coverage at 3 Hz, overlay on. serious: pick the 30 fps lowest-resolution ARConfiguration.VideoFormat at the next pause, coverage at 1 Hz, stop rendering the mesh overlay (keep collecting), stop hole computation, show 'Phone is warm, keep going but slow down'. critical: pause the session, save state, tell the user to wait 1-2 minutes. Also: isIdleTimerDisabled = true while scanning, warn at 4 minutes of continuous RoomPlan scanning (Apple: under 5 minutes), suggest splitting rooms, warn below 20% battery, enable battery monitoring and log batteryLevel every 30 s so you get a real %/min figure from the tester's phone.

Session quality log per scan (feeds both the UI and the accuracy formula): fraction of frames with trackingState != .normal, count of relocalizations, time spent under each RoomPlan Instruction, min/median ambientIntensity, thermalState timeline, RoomPlan CaptureError if any, per-wall completedEdges/confidence/coverage, and the depth-confidence histogram of counted observations. Store it next to the CapturedRoomData JSON.

Wall-thickness and drift honesty: because RoomPlan normalizes wall thickness (~16 cm) and drifts 0.5-2% over a room loop, present floor-plan dimensions as 'interior face to face' and label the plan accuracy class as 'estimated ±1 in per 10 ft' rather than per-wall millimetres.

Use RoomPlan's Instruction stream as the primary live coaching text during room scans (it is Apple-tuned and ~90% accurate); add your own only for what RoomPlan lacks: coverage percentage, the wall list with missing completedEdges, thermal warnings and the 5-minute timer.
open_questions: Does RoomCaptureSession's internally created (or user-supplied) ARSession run with sceneReconstruction = .meshWithClassification and frameSemantics containing .sceneDepth? Not documented. Verify on the first device build by logging `session.arSession.configuration` in captureSession(_:didStartWith:) and by counting ARMeshAnchors in the ARSessionDelegate. If it does not, the mesh coverage pass must run as a separate ARWorldTrackingConfiguration session (RoomPlan pass first, mesh pass second, or vice versa).
Exact runtime semantics of completedEdges (observed vs geometrically closed) and how quickly an edge flips to completed; only community evidence exists. Measure on device.
Can ARConfiguration.videoFormat be changed on the ARSession that RoomPlan drives without RoomPlan throwing invalidARConfiguration? Untested.
Real thermal timeline on an iPhone 13 Pro Max on iOS 18.3.2 with LiDAR + mesh overlay: minutes to .serious and .critical, and battery % per minute. No published numbers; collect from the session log.
ARMeshAnchor update cadence and anchor block extent on iOS 18 (community says roughly 0.5-1 s and about 1-2 m blocks); affects only the hole-computation budget.
Whether ARKit's confidenceMap on iOS 18 still uses raw values 0/1/2 with kCVPixelFormatType_OneComponent8 (Apple says read the format at runtime); assert it in a debug log on first run.

Whether Apple's 3.7 cm median ARKit-vs-Faro figure (ARKitScenes) is dominated by far-range pixels; if so the near-range depth term in the formula could be tightened after an on-device tape-measure calibration.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified this session from Apple's doc JSON. (1) roomplan/roomcapturesession/instruction.json: declaration `enum Instruction`, availability iOS 16.0 / iPadOS 16.0 / Mac Catalyst 16.0, no deprecation flags; the "Determining a coaching recommendation" topic section lists exactly six cases: normal, moveCloseToWall, moveAwayFromWall, turnOnLight, slowDown, lowTexture. Overview text confirms delivery via `captureSession(_:didProvide:)`. (2) roomplan/roomcapturesessiondelegate/capturesession(_:didprovide:).json: exact declaration `func captureSession(_ session: RoomCaptureSession, didProvide instruction: RoomCaptureSession.Instruction)`, iOS 16.0+, with a blank default implementation (so it is effectively optional to implement, a nuance the claim does not contradict). (3) roomplan/roomcapturesession/instruction/lowtexture.json discussion: fires when the user points at a solid-color wall, or the viewfinder contains no wall edges or other defining room shapes, matching the claim verbatim. (4) machinelearning.apple.com/research/roomplan: states "90 percent accuracy across all three detection tasks" for the lighting/distance/speed scan-condition models (inputs: luminance + 3D feature points for lighting; 3D linear velocity + 2D projection velocity for distance/speed); no lux/meter/speed thresholds are published, matching the claim. Minor note only: the delegate protocol has six methods in total (didStartWith, didAdd, didRemove, didChange, didUpdate, didProvide, didEndWith:error:), and visionOS is not listed in the availability array, consistent with the claim's iOS 16.0+ / Mac Catalyst 16.0+ statement. Nothing in the claim is wrong; no correction needed. Note: WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted (200/200), so cross-checks were done via direct WebFetch of official Apple pages only.

Attempted refutation of the semantics: Apple's Edge overview paragraph reads "Each Surface instance ... has a set (completedEdges) that contains one of each case in this enumeration", which taken literally would mean the set always holds all four edges and the coverage heuristic would be meaningless. However (a) the property is a Set named "completed", which only makes sense if it can be partial, and (b) a WWDC22 RoomPlan lounge Q&A (github.com/emin-grbo/WWDCLounges, wwdc22 object-capture-and-room-plan-lounge.md) has a developer reporting "0 values for CompletedEdges, PolygonCorners and PolygonEdges" inside didUpdate even at high confidence, proving the set can be empty/partial at runtime. GitHub code search found no other real-world Swift usage of completedEdges, so treat the coverage-score heuristic as unverified on device and gate it behind a runtime check (log completedEdges.count per wall on the first scans). Note for the architecture: completedEdges may be empty during didUpdate callbacks and only populated in the final CapturedRoom, so compute coverage from the processed/final room, not from intermediate updates.

Apple's doc metadata lists it as iOS 16.0, not 17.0 as the task assumed; polygonCorners and Section are the iOS 17 additions.

unverified_critical_claims: RoomCaptureSession delivers live CapturedRoom updates (didAdd/didChange/didUpdate/didRemove) during the scan, a final CapturedRoomData on didEndWith, and exposes/accepts an ARSession. Errors include deviceTooHot, exceedSceneSizeLimit, worldTrackingFailure. stop(pauseARSession:) (iOS 17) keeps the ARSession alive between rooms.

ARFrame.sceneDepth / smoothedSceneDepth give an ARDepthData with depthMap (Float32 metres, kCVPixelFormatType_DepthFloat32) and confidenceMap (OneComponent8, one ARConfidenceLevel raw value per pixel: low=0, medium=1, high=2). Enabled by adding .sceneDepth / .smoothedSceneDepth to ARConfiguration.frameSemantics after checking supportsFrameSemantics. Depth is 60 Hz, 256x192 (same aspect as the camera image); LiDAR range is about 5 m; confidence drops on highly reflective or highly absorbing surfaces.

Scene mesh: enable ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.sceneReconstruction = .meshWithClassification (check supportsSceneReconstruction first) and receive ARMeshAnchor via ARSessionDelegate session(_:didAdd:)/session(_:didUpdate:)/session(_:didRemove:). ARMeshGeometry exposes vertices, normals (per face), faces (triangles, ARGeometryElement) and an optional per-face classification buffer (UInt8 raw ARMeshClassification, 0 = .none). Mesh anchors 'constantly update' but are not real-time. ARSession.RunOptions.resetSceneReconstruction clears them. If plane detection is enabled ARKit flattens the mesh on detected planes.

ObjectCaptureSession.Feedback has exactly these cases: environmentLowLight, environmentTooDark, movingTooFast, objectNotDetected (iOS 17.4+), objectNotFlippable, objectTooClose, objectTooFar, outOfFieldOfView, overCapturing. There is NO 'outOfRange' case (the task's name is wrong; it is outOfFieldOfView). The session also exposes cameraTracking (normal/limited(reason:)/notAvailable), state, numberOfShotsTaken, maximumNumberOfInputImages, userCompletedScanPass, and AsyncSequence-style *Updates streams.

Screen projection for a live coverage overlay: on the iOS 26 SDK (Xcode 26.6) use ARCamera.projectPoint(_:orientation:viewportSize:), ARCamera.projectionMatrix(for:viewportSize:zNear:zFar:) and ARFrame.displayTransform(for:viewportSize:). Apple's doc marks the orientation-based variants deprecated only at iOS 27.0, replaced by viewRotationAngle variants that are iOS 27.0+ and therefore do NOT exist in the iOS 26 SDK. Do not use the viewRotationAngle APIs.

Thermal and battery APIs: ProcessInfo.processInfo.thermalState (nominal/fair/serious/critical) with ProcessInfo.thermalStateDidChangeNotification; isLowPowerModeEnabled; UIDevice.current.batteryLevel (requires isBatteryMonitoringEnabled = true); UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled. Apple's guidance for .serious is 'reduce target framerate 60 -> 30, reduce CPU/GPU work, lower detail'; for .critical 'if possible stop using peripherals such as the camera'. RoomPlan additionally ends the session with CaptureError.deviceTooHot.

Published iPhone LiDAR accuracy: small objects (>10 cm) ±1 cm absolute (Luetzenburg et al., Sci. Rep. 2021, iPhone 12 Pro); point-cloud RMSE vs known shapes 2.05 cm (iPhone 12 Pro) and 2.06 cm (iPhone 15) (Remote Sensing Letters 2026, tandfonline 10.1080/2150704X.2026.2720055); ARKit depth vs Faro ground truth agrees to 3.7 cm median (ARKitScenes analysis, rerun.io); reasonable accuracy up to about 4 m, noisy toward the ~5 m limit; building-scale scans with consumer apps put 69-83% of points within 5 cm of a terrestrial laser scan (iPhone 13 Pro, MDPI 2023); errors grow with distance and with path length because of SLAM drift.
